summary: Bulk transfer has no scope gate and audit fallback attributes the move to the TARGET rep when actorId is null (super_admin).
scenario: Super_admin with crmProfileId=null POSTs opportunityIds across entities; findMany has no scope filter, every ownerId is rewritten, and CrmActivityLog actorId falls back to toRepId (the receiving rep) — cross-tenant ownership writes with corrupted audit attribution.
recommended_fix: Apply scopeOpportunityByRole/per-row entity check inside the tx; replace actorId fallback with `actorId: null` and stamp actingAdminId from the real super_admin session id; record the original ownerId on each CrmActivityLog row.

summary: v11 'scope check added' is a no-op for MANAGER because scopeOpportunityByRole returns {} for MANAGER — any manager can trigger workflows on any opp and cascade notes+attachments into a downstream run.
scenario: MANAGER hits trigger-workflow with a foreign opp id; findFirst spreads {} scope so the row resolves, then 132-167 mirrors every CrmNote/CrmAttachment into TaskComment/TaskAttachment on a workflow run a downstream team can read.
recommended_fix: Pin the trigger-workflow findFirst to a per-call entity/scope clause derived from the opp (not the role rbac map), or AND an `entityId: session.user.crmEntityId` filter for MANAGER unless explicitly cross-entity.

summary: Drag-drop required-fields gate is a 6-case switch; the other 8 admin-configurable required keys silently bypass the gate.
scenario: Admin marks primaryContactId+description required on NEW; rep drags opp NEW→CONTACTED with both empty; the switch matches no case, `missing` stays [], move succeeds.
recommended_fix: Replace the switch with the generic `(opp as Record<string, unknown>)[field]` null/empty check used by actions.ts and bulk/route.ts; share one helper across all three surfaces.

summary: v11 added stage/priority/estimatedValueEGP/etc. to ClauseBuilder, but fire payloads never include these fields; engine reads payload only — every opp-field condition silently never matches.
scenario: Admin builds opp.stage.changed + priority=HOT rule; rep moves HOT opp; fireWorkflow payload omits priority; evalPredicate reads undefined; conditionOk=false; no run row, no notification, no error — lastFiredAt stays blank, admin assumes 'no events match yet.'
recommended_fix: Enrich fireWorkflow callsites to spread the full opp/cold-lead row (stage, priority, estimatedValueEGP, weightedValueEGP, probabilityPct, ownerId, entityId) into the payload, OR have the engine fetch the entity by entityType+entityId before evalPredicate.

summary: UI exposes 'amount'/'ageDays'/'attempts' fields that don't exist on the entities cron loads; every rule using these reads undefined and never fires.
scenario: Admin saves rule 'Value (EGP) > 50000' (key=amount); cron loads opps selecting estimatedValueEGP; readPath(payload,'amount')→undefined; gt returns false; rule silently dead.
recommended_fix: Rename UI field keys to match Prisma column names (estimatedValueEGP, etc.), compute ageDays in loadEntities, drop 'attempts' or add a real column. Add a save-time validator that fails any rule whose field paths aren't resolvable for its scope.

summary: Numeric operators require typeof==='number' on both sides, but Prisma Decimal columns are objects — every monetary clause silently evaluates false.
scenario: Rule {field:'estimatedValueEGP', op:'gt', value:50000}; cron loads Decimal; typeof===object; gt false for every opp.
recommended_fix: In loadEntities, coerce Decimal columns via Number(x) before passing into evalPredicate; or relax the type guard to accept Decimal/string-numeric via Number() with isFinite check.

summary: PATCH/DELETE status guard checks status==='approved' but bonus enum is pending/applied — guard never fires post-approval.
scenario: Bonus moves to 'applied' via approve; PATCH/DELETE comparator string-mismatches and update/delete proceeds on an already-applied bonus.
recommended_fix: Change comparison to `existing.status === 'applied'` (or `!== 'pending'`); add positive whitelist of permitted edits during pending and tests for every status value.

summary: Incident PATCH lets HR swap violation_rule / incident_date without recomputing actionTaken/deductionPct/deductionAmount/offenseNumber and without re-checking payroll-period lock.
scenario: Create incident for late_attendance (verbal_warning,0%); PATCH violation_rule to theft rule — row says theft but penalty stays 0; or PATCH incident_date into a locked period, no re-check.
recommended_fix: On PATCH, if violation_rule or incident_date change, re-derive offenseNumber/action/deduction via the same path used by POST, and re-run the payroll-period lock check; or refuse to PATCH these two fields and require delete+recreate.

summary: v11 canAccessCompany rollout missed payroll/calculate POST — accountant in Company A can recalc Company B.
scenario: POST {company_id: companyB_id} with role=accountant; canManagePayroll passes globally; no company-scope guard; calculateCompanyPayroll runs on the wrong tenant.
recommended_fix: Add `if (!canAccessCompany(authUser, company_id)) return 403` immediately after canManagePayroll.

summary: Per-row salary recalc has no canAccessCompany — any accountant can rewrite any open salary cross-tenant.
scenario: POST /salaries/<companyB_id>/recalculate; status='open' passes; calculateEmployeeSalary + update writes Company B figures.
recommended_fix: Load salary including employee.companyId; `if (!canAccessCompany(authUser, salary.employee.companyId)) return 403`.

summary: GET scope filter overwritten by ?company= — spread+overwrite defeats the v11 in-clause scope.
scenario: Accountant of Company A hits ?company=companyB_id; the `where.employee.companyId` `{in:[...]}` is replaced by the literal companyB_id.
recommended_fix: Build where.employee as a merge: keep the `in` filter, and AND the optional ?company= filter only if the value is inside authUser.companies.

summary: Meeting PATCH accepts arbitrary status and bypasses approve/deny/complete state machine — rep can self-APPROVE or jump to DONE.
scenario: REP PATCHes {status:'APPROVED'} on own meeting; loadOrError allows scheduler; patchSchema accepts; update writes APPROVED with approvedById=null.
recommended_fix: Drop status from patchSchema (or whitelist only 'CANCELLED'); funnel every transition through /approve, /deny, /complete endpoints that enforce role + state.

summary: Attendance log PATCH bypasses v11's cross-company gate, hour clamp, and payroll-lock check — all applied only to POST.
scenario: PATCH a Company B log with hours_worked=999, overtime=999, date in a PAID period; isHROrAdmin passes; raw parseFloat writes.
recommended_fix: Port the three POST guards verbatim into PATCH: canAccessCompany on the existing log's employee.companyId, period-lock check on data.date or existing.date, Math.min(24,Math.max(0,...)) clamp.

summary: Overnight checkout still keys on today's midnight, so the night-shift row from yesterday is never found — v11 'fix' is dead code.
scenario: Check-in 22:30 on D-1 → row date=D-1; check-out 06:15 on D → findUnique on date=D returns null → 400 'no check-in record.'
recommended_fix: Either look up the most recent unclosed log for the employee (status='present' AND checkOutTime IS NULL) regardless of date, or fall back to yesterday's row when today is empty.

summary: Shared isPlatformAdmin still admits partners-admin — only impersonate POST was tightened, so partners-admin can reset super_admin password, grant themselves modules, etc.
scenario: User with modules=['partners'], partnerId=null POSTs /api/admin/users/<superAdmin>/reset-password; isPlatformAdmin OR-branch passes; sets a new password; logs in as super_admin.
recommended_fix: Tighten the shared helper to `hrRoles?.includes('super_admin')` only; remove every inline duplicate (admin/board/users/[id]/modules/reset-password/services-catalogue/workflows/sequential-workflows/etc.) and import the helper.

summary: Convert TOCTOU loser still orphans CrmCompany and CrmContact rows — only the opportunity is soft-archived.
scenario: Two concurrent converts on lead L; both find no company → both create; both create contact; both create opp; loser's updateMany count=0; only opp is soft-deleted; orphan company+contact persist.
recommended_fix: Wrap company find-or-create + contact create + createOpportunity inside the same $transaction; on count=0 race-loser branch, also delete the company (if it was just created by this tx) and the contact.

summary: Re-WON commission upsert overwrites already-PAID commission with new amount but keeps status=PAID, destroying audit trail.
scenario: Deal WON→LOST→WON (value 10x); existing commission row {amount:100, status:PAID} is upserted to {amount:1000, status:PAID} — no second row, no history of original $100 payout.
recommended_fix: On WON re-entry, if commission exists with status APPROVED/PAID, leave it intact and create a new commission delta row (or refuse the rate/value change without admin override); always reset status to PENDING when amount changes.
